summary: Amrita Saikia works in Tibetology and other fields. She earned her PhD from the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (2018–2022) and held positions there, as Assistant Professor at Woxsen University (2022), and as Visiting Fellow at GIGA (2023–2024).

Amrith Krishna works in linguistics and Indology. He has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, University of Cambridge, IT University of Copenhagen, Oriflow, Uniphore (attested 2023), and Learno.AI (attested 2024–2025).
Amruta Barbadikar specializes in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. She completed her PhD at the University of Hyderabad in 2020 and has held a post there.

Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist. She earned degrees from Barnard, INALCO, and a PhD from the EPHE under Ariane Macdonald, later holding posts at Yale, CNRS, Sapienza University of Rome, SOAS, INALCO, and the University of Bern.

Amy L. Allocco specializes in religious studies and Indology. She studied at Colgate University, Harvard University, and Emory University (PhD 2001–2009), and was affiliated with Elon University (attested 2015).

Amy Paris Langenberg works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University and was appointed assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College around 2014.

Amy Sims Miller works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Wesleyan University and completed her MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano, alongside numerous traditional teachers including Geshe Jampel Thardo and Janice Dean Willis.

Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar of linguistics and Japanology. She earned degrees from the University of California, Los Angeles in 1990 and 1993, and became a professor at the University of Washington around 1995.
Ana Agud is a linguist and Indologist. She studied at the University of Salamanca (PhD 1965–1978) and the University of Tübingen, and became a professor at the University of Salamanca in 1979.

Anagarika Dharmapala (1864–1933) was a religious studies and Buddhist studies figure. Educated at schools in Colombo including S. Thomas' College and Royal College, he founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Anagarika Govinda (1898–1985) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a doctorate at the University of Freiburg, founded the Arya Maitreya Mandala in 1933, and taught at Visva-Bharati, Patna, and other Indian universities.

Anagarika Munindra (1915–2003) was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher. He studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and Satya Narayan Goenka, and served as superintendent of the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957.
Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Tsurlo Rinpoche and has served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

Anand A. Yang is a historian and Indologist. He studied at Swarthmore College and the University of Virginia, and held posts at Sweet Briar College, the University of Utah, and the University of Washington (around 2002).

Anand Venkatkrishnan specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctoral degree from Columbia University in 2015 and serves as Assistant Professor of the History of Religion in South Asia at the University of Chicago.

Ananda Guruge (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Ceylon and University of London (PhD), and held posts at NIEPA, California State University, Fullerton, and University of the West.

Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy (1877–1947) was an Indologist, art historian, and philosopher. Educated at UCL and the University of London (D.Sc.), he directed the Mineral Survey of Ceylon and served as Keeper and Fellow at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

Anant Sadashiv Altekar (1898–1959) was an Indologist and historian. He served as professor and department head at Banaras Hindu University (ca. 1930–1949), university professor at Patna University (ca. 1949–1957), and director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute.

Anantalal Thakur (1916–2009) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta and under Satkari Mookerjee. He held professorships at the Mithila Institute and served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).

Anantanand Rambachan works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of the West Indies, under Dayananda Saraswati, and at the University of Leeds, and was a long-serving professor at St. Olaf College (ca. 1985–2021).
